title: Peg a T-shirt onto a clothesline
instruction: Hang the T-shirt from the clothesline using the two pegs, then let go and leave it secure and clear of the table.
context: Clipping flexible clothing onto a line combines fabric handling with operating a spring clamp, a common household and assisted-living activity.
setup: Proposed fixed setup, metres in the YAM station frame: a dry cotton child-sized T-shirt, body width 0.28, hem-to-shoulder length 0.30, sleeve span 0.40, nominal 180 g/m² and 33.9 g, lies flat with hem at x=0.18 and shoulders at x=0.48, centred at y=0 on the 0.7475 m high table. A taut 3 mm line spans y=-0.25 to +0.25 at x=0.52,z=1.09, supported by two fixed 25 mm square posts and 150 x 70 x 15 mm feet. Two 70 x 10 x 22 mm wooden spring pegs, nominal 8 g each, start closed at x=0.12,y=+/-0.20,z=0.7615, long axes along x. Final screenshot and reachable layout require physical validation.
scoring: Proposed: 0.5 for one peg visibly retaining the hem and line, with the whole shirt at least 20 mm clear of the table/floor and unsupported by the robot for 5 seconds; 1.0 for two such pegs at least 180 mm apart. Otherwise 0. Damaged objects, false contact, hidden attachments or unphysical deformation invalidate the run. See JUDGING.md.
run_limit: Proposed: 2,400 control steps, 2 minutes at 20 Hz, including the final 5-second released hold.
reset_notes: Restore the flat dry garment, closed pegs and fixed rack to the stated layout. Replace damaged physical fabric or pegs. Final reset has not been validated.
fidelity: Implemented native 2D surface FEM with two sewn fabric layers, self-contact and passive spring-driven rigid jaws. No proximity grasp or cloth animation. Taut line is a static cylinder. Cotton anisotropy, yarns, tearing and wetness are not modeled. Friction, bending and peg torque are uncalibrated; no GPU run yet.
scores: Not evaluated. No demo or Dream score exists.
